title: Weil extension into a smooth separated relative group scheme
statement: Let $S$ be a normal Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning it has a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings and every local ring is an integrally closed domain. Let $p:Z\to S$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $H\to S$ be a smooth separated group scheme. Here a group scheme has multiplication, identity and inverse morphisms over $S$ satisfying the group identities; separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $U\subseteq Z$ be an open subscheme and $u:U\to H$ an $S$-morphism. Suppose $U_s\subseteq Z_s$ is dense for every $s\in S$, where the fibres are base changes to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], and suppose $U$ contains every $z\in Z$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{Z,z}\leq1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then there is a unique $S$-morphism $\bar u:Z\to H$ restricting to $u$. Neither $Z$ nor $H$ is required to be quasi-compact, and the group need not be commutative or have connected fibres.

source.place: BLR §4.4 Theorem 1, printed pp.109–110 (PDF pp.115–116), applied locally on the source; primary scan read online, local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Work first on an affine open $T\subseteq Z$ mapping into an affine open $S_0\subseteq S$. Its restricted structural map is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. Since $S_0$ is normal, [lem-sfb-smooth-normal-ascent] makes $T$ normal. Since $S_0$ is reduced and locally Noetherian, [lem-trf-smooth-reduced-dense-pullback] makes $T$ reduced and locally Noetherian; being affine it is Noetherian. Put $U_T=U\cap T$. It is dense in $T$: every generic point of an affine irreducible component has a zero-dimensional local ring and hence lies in $U_T$. This argument also applies to every open subset of $T$. The local-ring dimension condition is unchanged on open restriction.

source.place: BLR §4.4, proof of Theorem 1, printed pp.109–110 (PDF pp.115–116), reduction to the diagonal; primary scan https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $P=T\times_{S_0}T$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ and diagonal $a:T\to P$. Both projections are smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. The open $D=U_T\times_{S_0}U_T=p_1^{-1}(U_T)\cap p_2^{-1}(U_T)$ is dense in $P$: [lem-trf-smooth-reduced-dense-pullback] makes each inverse image dense, and the intersection of two dense opens is dense. Define the $S_0$-morphism $g:D\to H_{S_0}$ by $g(z_1,z_2)=u(z_1)u(z_2)^{-1}$, using the given multiplication and inverse. We have $a^{-1}D=U_T$, and $g\circ a=e\circ p$ there, by the inverse identity. The target is separated over $S_0$: its diagonal is the restriction of the given closed diagonal, still a closed immersion because restricting a quotient on affine charts is a quotient.

source.place: BLR §4.4, proof of Theorem 1, printed pp.109–110 (PDF pp.115–116), reduction to the diagonal; primary scan https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-section-rational-extension] with $B=S_0$, the normal Noetherian $T$ of step 1, $X=P$, $q=p_1$, section $a$, target $Y=H_{S_0}$, $v=g$, and $b=e\circ p$. The dense domain and equality along $a$ are step 2; $a^{-1}D=U_T$ contains all the required points by hypothesis. Obtain an open $V\subseteq P$ containing $a(T)$ and a morphism $v:V\to H_{S_0}$ agreeing with $g$ on $V\cap D$. This is precisely the codimension argument of the source; it is isolated in the cited lemma, not assumed from the definition of a rational map.

source.place: BLR §4.4, proof of Theorem 1, printed pp.109–110 (PDF pp.115–116), reduction to the diagonal; primary scan https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Let $W=V\cap p_2^{-1}(U_T)$ and $f=p_1|_W:W\to T$. It is smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes], hence flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat], and open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. It is surjective: for $z\in T$ over $s\in S_0$, the fibre $V_z$ is a nonempty open of $T_s\times_{\kappa(s)}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)$, since it contains the diagonal point. The projection of this latter scheme to $T_s$ is open by [lem-sc-scheme-over-field-universally-open]. Thus the image of $V_z$ is a nonempty open meeting the dense $U_{T,s}$; a point over that intersection lies in $W_z$. (The open $U_{T,s}$ is dense in the open $T_s\subset Z_s$ by the original fibrewise density.) Consequently $f$ is an fpqc cover in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]: on each affine open of $T$, affine opens of its inverse image have open images covering it, so quasi-compactness selects finitely many.

source.place: BLR §4.4, proof of Theorem 1, printed pp.109–110 (PDF pp.115–116), reduction to the diagonal; primary scan https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Define $h:W\to H_{S_0}$ by $h(z_1,z_2)=v(z_1,z_2)u(z_2)$. On $f^{-1}(U_T)$ both coordinates lie in $U_T$, so $v=g$ and $h=(u\circ p_1)u(z_2)^{-1}u(z_2)=u\circ f$, with parentheses moved by associativity. No commutativity is used. On $C=W\times_T W$ compare $h\circ\operatorname{pr}_1$ and $h\circ\operatorname{pr}_2$. The schemes $W$ and $C$ are reduced and locally Noetherian, and the inverse image of $U_T$ is dense in each, by two successive applications of [lem-trf-smooth-reduced-dense-pullback]: $W\to T$ and $C\to W$ are smooth, the latter by [lem-pc-proper-base-change]. Over that dense open the two maps equal $u$ after the common map to $T$. Therefore [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext] makes them equal everywhere on $C$.

source.place: BLR §4.4, proof of Theorem 1, printed pp.109–110 (PDF pp.115–116), reduction to the diagonal; primary scan https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: The compatibility from step 5 and the fpqc covering from step 4 allow [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to descend $h$ uniquely to $\bar u_T:T\to H$. It is an $S$-morphism: its structural composite and $p|_T$ agree after $f$, so the uniqueness clause of that same descent statement, with target $S$, identifies them. Restricting the covering to $U_T$, the identity $h=u\circ f$ shows $\bar u_T|_{U_T}=u|_{U_T}$, again by uniqueness in descent. The restricted covering is fpqc by the same finite-affine-image argument as in step 4.

source.place: BLR §4.4, proof of Theorem 1, printed pp.109–110 (PDF pp.115–116), reduction to the diagonal; primary scan https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~kamenova/homepage_files/Bosch_Raynaud_Neron_Model_tc.pdf read online; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: Perform the construction on all such affine neighbourhoods $T$ of $Z$. On an overlap $T\cap T\prime$, the two morphisms agree on $U\cap T\cap T\prime$, dense because it contains all generic points; the overlap is reduced by step 1. Relative separatedness and [lem-sfb-relative-separated-dominant-ext] give equality on the overlap. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] glues them to an $S$-morphism $\bar u:Z\to H$ restricting to $u$. Two extensions agree by the same relative separatedness lemma on the dense open $U$ in the reduced $Z$. All covers may be infinite. If $Z$ is empty, its unique morphism is the required extension; empty fibres caused no condition in step 4.
